what_happened: The job split the athena-core --lib tests into filtered parts across CI test shards. It was rejected at the final verdict. The verifier reported one major finding: clippy fails on the new test file xtask/tests/shard_parts.rs at lines 139-142, so the "tested" default (clippy clean) is broken. One check failed, `clippy`. A check is not a criterion, and the event lists no unmet acceptance criteria. The sharding work itself is not reported as faulty.
cause: Nothing requires the producer to run the full gate (fmt, clippy --all-targets, test) on the files it adds, and see it pass, before it finishes. A new test file is checked by clippy only at the final verification, so a lint warning in it shows up as a rejection rather than a quick fix. There is also no cheap repair step for a mechanical lint defect. Rejection is the only outcome once the verifier finds it. This is an inference, since the stored fields do not show the producer's report or the lint text.
prevention: Add a pre-verdict gate in the job pipeline. After the producer stops, Athena itself runs fmt --check and clippy --all-targets -D warnings (and test) on the job's snapshot. If any fail, it sends the exact output back to the producer for one repair round within the same job. The verifier is only started once the gate is clean. That would have caught the clippy failure at xtask/tests/shard_parts.rs:139-142 and fixed it before judging.
proposed_request: Add a pre-verification lint gate to the job pipeline. After the producer finishes and before the verifier starts, Athena runs `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on the job's working copy. If either fails, it passes the failing output back to the producer for one repair round in the same job and runs the gate again. Only a clean gate proceeds to the verifier. If the gate is still red after the repair round, the job ends failed with the gate output recorded as the reason. Acceptance: (1) a test with a fixture producer that leaves a clippy warning in a new test file shows the output is sent back and the job continues after the repair; (2) a test shows a job whose gate is still red after the repair round ends failed with the output recorded and the verifier never started; (3) a clean job is unchanged; (4) a CHANGELOG entry; (5) fmt, clippy and the full cargo test pass for the workspace.
